## Statute
§68(b)(1)(C) - "$250,000 in the case of an individual who is not married and who is not a surviving spouse or head of household"
§68(b)(1)(B) - "$275,000 in the case of a head of household (as defined in section 2(b))"
§68(f) - "This section shall not apply to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026."

## Reasoning
Section 68(b)(1)(C) specifically applies to "an individual who is not married and who is not a surviving spouse or head of household." Alice is explicitly stated to be a head of household for 2016. Therefore, Section 68(b)(1)(C) does NOT apply to Alice - instead, Section 68(b)(1)(B) would apply to her, which sets the applicable amount at $275,000 for heads of household. Additionally, Section 68(f) confirms Section 68 applies to 2016 (taxable years before January 1, 2018). The claim that Section 68(b)(1)(C) applies to Alice is false because she is a head of household, which is explicitly excluded from 68(b)(1)(C).

## Answer
Answer: Contradiction
